appraisal_events.evidence: « Vous avez tort, dit Mme de Guermantes, avec des longueurs insupportables Wagner avait du génie. Lohengrin est un chef-d'œuvre... le Chœur des fileuses du Vaisseau fantôme est une pure merveille. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess directly contradicts her husband's self-declared old-fashioned taste and asserts her own more discerning judgment of Wagner, correcting him in front of company.

appraisal_events.evidence: « ...gardez cela pour un jour où Mémé sera là. Lui, c'est encore mieux, il le sait par cœur. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The speaker defers the topic in favor of Charlus, praising his superior expertise on Balzac even though Charlus is absent from the scene.

status_effects.explanation: His declared taste is openly corrected by his wife in company, mildly undercutting his stated critical position.
She asserts confident, specific critical judgments about Wagner, positioning her taste as more discerning than her husband's in this exchange.
Charlus is elevated by reputation as an even greater authority on Balzac than the duc, despite not being present in the scene.

ambiguities: The speaker of the final line ('Ah! mon cher, si vous partez en guerre sur Balzac...') is not explicitly tagged; it most plausibly continues M. de Bréauté's exchange with the duc (who had just addressed him as 'Babal'), but this attribution is inferred rather than stated in the text.
